reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 18:1-6 = MT 18:2-7; Ps 18 is a shift+1 psalm and the row's dual-cite web:Ps.18.0 = oshb:Ps.18.1 is arithmetically correct against the offset map and both verse maps (oshb:Ps.18.1 carries is_counted_title true, web Ps.18.0). Title-as-opening-row evidence is owner-ruled admissible, so the form is not at issue. Both Hebrew runs in the row are quotation-grade: collate.py returns tier byte for each against oshb:Ps.18.1. Disclosure obligations are clear - the selah inventory holds 0 verses in Ps 18 out of 71 book-wide, and the only Ps 18 ketiv/qere note sits at oshb:Ps.18.51, outside this span, so nothing is owed here. The closing seam is byte-warranted independently of the row's prose: MT 18:8 opens the waw-prefixed scene shift וַתִּגְעַ֬שׁ against the answered-cry close of MT 18:7. The span itself I do not contest. Two defects sit in the title sentence: a positional claim about the Hebrew that the bytes contradict, and a count whose object is not reproducible as stated. Flagged but NOT filed: the device note calls 2 Samuel 22 both a prose parallel and a typed cross-book relation. The declared typed-relation set in this campaign is cross-psalm - the 3 doublets plus the 9-10 pair - and no cross-book relation type is carried by pmarks_Ps.json or psalm_device_inventory.json, so typed asserts a registry status the in-scope inventories do not certify, and prose is a genre claim about a text I cannot reach from in-scope sources. Because I cannot evidence 2 Samuel from the permitted toolkit, filing it would breach the symmetric evidence rule; I record it for the assembler instead.

challenges.claim: The row states the title opens with לְעֶ֥בֶד יְהוָ֗ה, but that phrase stands at words 2-3 of the 20 whitespace-separated tokens of oshb:Ps.18.1; the title opens with לַמְנַצֵּ֤חַ.
challenges.evidence: Spliced byte-true from verse_map_oshb.json (never retyped); oshb:Ps.18.1 = web:Ps.18.0 under the shift+1 rule (title = MT v1). Token 1 of 20: לַמְנַצֵּ֤חַ . Tokens 2-3: לְעֶ֥בֶד יְהוָ֗ה . Tokens 19-20: וּמִיַּ֥ד שָׁאֽוּל . The quoted run begins at character index 13 of the verse, not 0; startswith returns False. collate.py --ref oshb:Ps.18.1 returns tier byte for both of the row's runs, so this is a positional error, not a fidelity error - which is why it survived the quote checkers. The row's own WEB quotation in the same sentence carries the correct order: “For the Chief Musician. By David the servant of Yahweh,” (web:Ps.18.0). The closes-with half of the claim is TRUE: וּמִיַּ֥ד שָׁאֽוּל occupies tokens 19-20 of 20. The opening token is also the psalm-device inventory's own basis for counting Ps 18 among the 55 lamnatseach superscriptions, so the row's reading of the opening contradicts the inventory it otherwise relies on.

challenges.claim: The parenthetical sweep citation of 20 words names a unit sweep.py does not emit and an object the maqaf-free staged source view cannot certify as MT words.
challenges.evidence: The digit is reproducible in one sense only: oshb:Ps.18.1 splits into 20 whitespace-separated tokens in the staged extract (20 tokens, 1 verse). But sweep.py's units are VERSE counts by default and token-occurrence counts under --tokens, always for a query string swept book-wide; it exposes no per-verse word-count mode, so no sweep.py invocation yields 20 words. And the staged OSHB extract serializes maqaf as a space - 0 maqaf codepoints book-wide against 2404 x-maqqef segs in the OSHB XML - so whitespace tokens and Masoretic accentual words are two different objects in this book and the row names neither. Per count-object discipline the citation must name the swept object (whitespace tokens of the staged view) and its unit, or drop the sweep attribution. Nothing else in the row turns on the figure, hence low.

reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 18:7-10 = MT 18:8-11, dual-cite arithmetic clean under shift+1. The row quotes no Hebrew, so there is nothing to collate; its English quotations are verbatim against verse_map_web.json. The selah note is span-scoped and true: the pmarks selah inventory holds 71 verses book-wide and 0 of them fall in Ps 18. No paseq, inverted-nun or suspended-letter claim is made - the paseq inventory does list MT 18:7, 18:8 and 18:9, seg layer and single-witness, and the row correctly leaves it alone rather than dressing it up as boundary evidence. I tested the closing seam at WEB 18:10|18:11 = MT 18:11|18:12 independently and it holds on morphosyntax the row does not cite: MT 18:8-11 run a waw-prefixed narrative chain (וַתִּגְעַ֬שׁ ... וַיֵּ֣ט ... וַיִּרְכַּ֣ב), and MT 18:12 opens asyndetically with the prefix form יָ֤שֶׁת - so the row's imagery argument lands on a real break rather than an arbitrary one. I weighed the rival that the whole theophany MT 18:8-16 is one indivisible unit, since בְּאַפּ֗וֹ at MT 18:9 and אַפֶּֽךָ at MT 18:16 bracket it on a shared lexeme; that bracket argues for a larger movement but not against a strophe seam inside it, and row-policy expressly permits strophe rows in a long psalm, so it is not a challenge. Confidence medium is calibrated for a seam argued from imagery clustering rather than from a frame. No defect found.

Span WEB 18:11-15 = MT 18:12-16. Selah note span-scoped and true (0 selah verses in Ps 18). The row's load-bearing claim - that second-person address returns at the close of WEB 18:15 - is byte-true at MT 18:16, which carries the 2ms forms מִגַּעֲרָ֣תְךָ֣ and אַפֶּֽךָ (web:Ps.18.15 = oshb:Ps.18.16), after MT 18:3-15 run without 2ms reference to the deity; the WEB wording the row leans on, “at your rebuke, Yahweh” (web:Ps.18.15), is faithful to those bytes. Internal cohesion is stronger than the row claims and confirms the span: the closing three tokens of MT 18:13 and of MT 18:14 are BYTE-identical - בָּ֝רָ֗ד וְגַֽחֲלֵי אֵֽשׁ at both, collate tier byte, 3 tokens across 2 verses - a repeated colon wholly inside this span, which is a better unity argument than the vocabulary-cluster signal the row filed. The opening seam holds for the reason given on the adjacent row: the waw-chain of MT 18:8-11 stops at the asyndetic יָ֤שֶׁת. On the closing seam I note, without filing it here, that the waters lexeme straddles it (מַ֗יִם at MT 18:16 against מִמַּ֥יִם at MT 18:17); this row's prose asserts no imagery break at that seam, so the disclosure debt belongs to the row that does assert one, and I file it there rather than twice. No defect found.

Span WEB 18:16-19 = MT 18:17-20. Selah note span-scoped and true. The seam PLACEMENT I do not contest: MT 18:21 opens the retribution unit cleanly and the row discloses the causal hinge at its own close. What fails is the warrant's characterisation of the span, which is derived from the WEB rendering and does not survive the MT. Two problems, one filed. Filed: the row asserts the span has no theophanic imagery of its own at exactly the seam where the bytes repeat the theophany's own waters lexeme. Recorded as an observation rather than a filed challenge: the row calls the sequence a chain of finite past-tense action verbs, but at MT 18:17-18 and 18:20 the forms are prefix-conjugation (יִשְׁלַ֣ח, יִקָּחֵ֑נִי, יַֽ֝מְשֵׁ֗נִי, יַצִּילֵ֗נִי, יְקַדְּמ֥וּנִי, יְ֝חַלְּצֵ֗נִי), while וַֽיְהִי and וַיּוֹצִיאֵ֥נִי are waw-consecutive; past-tense is a property of WEB's English, not of these bytes, and the morphological contrast in fact runs opposite to the prior strophe's waw-chain. I leave that as an observation because a preterite reading of the prefix forms is defensible in translation-facing prose. Confidence high is not supportable while the span's stated distinguishing property is falsified in its own opening verse.

challenges.claim: The warrant's absence claim - that the span carries no theophanic imagery of its own - is falsified in the row's own opening verse, which repeats the waters lexeme of the immediately preceding verse across the row's own seam, undisclosed.
challenges.evidence: web:Ps.18.15 = oshb:Ps.18.16 and web:Ps.18.16 = oshb:Ps.18.17 (shift+1). Spliced byte-true: MT 18:16 reads אֲפִ֥יקֵי מַ֗יִם and MT 18:17 reads מִמַּ֥יִם רַבִּֽים - the same waters lexeme in two attested spellings, which must be swept per spelling: the two verses share 0 tokens at byte, accent_stripped AND skeleton tier, so no single sweep joins them. Naming the object and unit: a contiguous consonantal sweep of the waters consonants over Ps 18 returns 10 tokens over 10 verses, of which only 3 tokens over 3 verses are the waters lexeme (MT 18:12, 18:16, 18:17 = web:Ps.18.11, 18:15, 18:16); the other 7 are homograph collisions with the heavens, blameless and peoples tokens (שָׁ֭מַיִם MT 18:10, בַּשָּׁמַ֨יִם MT 18:14, תָמִ֣ים MT 18:24, תָּ֝מִ֗ים MT 18:26, תָּמִ֪ים MT 18:31, תָּמִ֣ים MT 18:33, עַמִּ֣ים MT 18:48). So the lexeme runs out of the theophany and across this row's opening seam into the very verse the row quotes. WEB shows the same continuity the row denies: “Then the channels of waters appeared.” (web:Ps.18.15) then “He drew me out of many waters.” (web:Ps.18.16). The same verse also opens “He sent from on high.” (web:Ps.18.16) = יִשְׁלַ֣ח מִ֭מָּרוֹם at oshb:Ps.18.17, a height locution that is theophanic-spatial rather than neutral rescue vocabulary. Under cross-seam cohesion the straddling device must be disclosed on both sides in one edit, or the absence claim withdrawn; as written the row denies the continuity its own quoted clause instantiates.

reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 18:20-24 = MT 18:21-25. Selah note span-scoped and true. Both seams are right and the inclusio the row rests on is REAL - I re-derived it rather than trusting the row: MT 18:21 and MT 18:25 share 3 of the 7 tokens of MT 18:21 at byte tier (יְהוָ֣ה, כְּבֹ֥ר, יָ֝דַ֗י) plus 2 of 7 more at skeleton tier (כְּצִדְקִ֑י against כְצִדְקִ֑י, and לִֽי against לִ֣י), 5 of the 7 tokens of MT 18:21 matching a token of the 8 in MT 18:25 at skeleton tier. So this verdict is not about the warrant's substance but about its precision - and precision is exactly what an inclusio claim trades on. The row describes the device as a restatement in which both verses open with the same clause; that description is false at the MT and inexact at the WEB, and the true figure is a chiastic hinge that is a stronger warrant than the one filed. I considered and rejected a second challenge on the 039|040 seam: the psalmist's self-description at MT 18:24 (תָמִ֣ים) is picked up at MT 18:26 (תָּ֝מִ֗ים) at skeleton tier, a straddle - but the adjacent row does disclose that link conceptually as a generalisation from the psalmist's own case, so the debt is paid and I do not file it. Confidence high is defensible for the span once the device is described correctly.

challenges.claim: The row's stated evidence - that web:Ps.18.20 and web:Ps.18.24 both open with the same clause and that the later verse restates the earlier one nearly word for word - is false at the MT, where the two verses open with different verbs, and inexact at the WEB; the actual device is a chiastic hinge.
challenges.evidence: web:Ps.18.20 = oshb:Ps.18.21 and web:Ps.18.24 = oshb:Ps.18.25 (shift+1). Spliced byte-true: MT 18:21 opens יִגְמְלֵ֣נִי and MT 18:25 opens וַיָּֽשֶׁב - different verbs sharing no skeleton. What actually happens is anadiplosis in chiasm: the closing two tokens of MT 18:21 are יָשִׁ֥יב לִֽי and the opening three tokens of MT 18:25 are וַיָּֽשֶׁב יְהוָ֣ה לִ֣י - the verb plus preposition that CLOSES the earlier member OPENS the later one, while the opening verb of the earlier member has no counterpart anywhere in the later one. The English identity the row leans on is a rendering artifact: WEB renders both verbs with reward/recompense, so “Yahweh has rewarded me according to my righteousness.” (web:Ps.18.20) and “Therefore Yahweh has rewarded me according to my righteousness,” (web:Ps.18.24) look alike in English while diverging at the bytes. Even on the WEB side both open is wrong: web:Ps.18.24 opens with Therefore. Under tier discipline, restatement-class wording requires the collate tier named; here the byte tier gives 3 of 7 shared tokens and no tier supports a restatement claim. The repair is to state the inclusio on the shared tokens and name the chiastic hinge, which costs the row nothing and gains it a sharper warrant.

reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 18:25-30 = MT 18:26-31. Selah note span-scoped and true; refs and dual-cite arithmetic clean; and the row's epithet-echo claim is byte-true as far as it goes, since MT 18:31 carries מָגֵ֥ן whose lexeme answers מָֽגִנִּ֥י at MT 18:3. The problem is that those facts pull the row's closing verse into the next row. The row itself concedes the direction of travel - it says the closing confession pivots toward the battle-equipping strophe that follows - and then keeps the verse anyway. Four independent tier-1 signals put the seam one verse earlier at WEB 18:29|18:30 = MT 18:30|18:31, and the row's own closing evidence phrase turns out to be the opening member of a collocation whose second member sits in the next row. I rate this high rather than medium because it is not a taste dispute about strophe length, which the policy would not entertain: a verse-initial particle lattice, a repeated divine designation, a repeated collocation and a bounding epithet converge on the same alternative, the row's own warrant already describes the verse as forward-facing, and the alternative leaves both rows policy-compliant at WEB 18:25-29 and WEB 18:30-36. Confidence medium is at least honest about the softness of the seam as filed.

challenges.claim: A better-warranted rival seam sits one verse earlier at WEB 18:29|18:30 = MT 18:30|18:31: the row's closing verse is the asyndetic head of the next movement, and holding it here severs a divine-designation frame, a repeated collocation and a bounding epithet that belong to the following strophe.
challenges.evidence: Refs dual-cited under shift+1: web:Ps.18.29 = oshb:Ps.18.30, web:Ps.18.30 = oshb:Ps.18.31, web:Ps.18.31 = oshb:Ps.18.32, web:Ps.18.32 = oshb:Ps.18.33, web:Ps.18.35 = oshb:Ps.18.36. Hebrew spliced byte-true from verse_map_oshb.json. (1) VERSE-INITIAL PARTICLE LATTICE, first token of each verse MT 18:26-33: עִם / עִם / כִּֽי / כִּֽי / כִּֽי / הָאֵל֮ / כִּ֤י / הָ֭אֵל . Object and unit named: 4 verses in MT 18:26-34 open with the causal particle (MT 18:28, 18:29, 18:30, 18:32 = 4 verses), and MT 18:31 is the SOLE asyndetic opener inside that run - the syntactic break falls before it, not after it. The three-fold anaphora at MT 18:28-30 closes the preceding movement on its own. (2) The particle opening MT 18:32 binds BACKWARD to MT 18:31, and WEB preserves the connective: “He is a shield to all those who take refuge in him.” (web:Ps.18.30) then “For who is God, except Yahweh?” (web:Ps.18.31) - the row's seam therefore separates a grounding clause from what it grounds. (3) DIVINE-DESIGNATION FRAME: MT 18:31 and MT 18:33 open with the same designation (הָאֵל֮ / הָ֭אֵל), identical at accent_stripped tier and differing at byte tier by accent placement only; the form occurs at 3 tokens over 3 verses in Ps 18 (MT 18:31, 18:33, 18:48), heading a participial epithet at 18:33 and 18:48 - so MT 18:31 and 18:33 frame the question at MT 18:32 between two members of one formula, and the row cuts the frame in half. (4) REPEATED COLLOCATION ACROSS THE ROW'S OWN SEAM: the row's closing evidence phrase is תָּמִ֪ים דַּ֫רְכּ֥וֹ at MT 18:31, and MT 18:33 closes with תָּמִ֣ים דַּרְכִּֽי - the same two-lexeme collocation, shared at accent_stripped tier, split by the boundary. WEB carries it too: “As for God, his way is perfect.” (web:Ps.18.30) against “and makes my way perfect?” (web:Ps.18.32). (5) BOUNDING EPITHET: the absolute form מָגֵ֥ן occurs at 2 tokens over 2 verses in Ps 18, MT 18:31 and MT 18:36 (מָגֵ֪ן יִ֫שְׁעֶ֥ךָ), swept as its own spelling since the suffixed form at MT 18:3 is a distinct spelling under final-letter allography and does not match it - so MT 18:31-36 = WEB 18:30-35 is bounded by that epithet, which is exactly the unit the rival seam produces. No tier-3 or tier-4 material is load-bearing: the paseq inventory does list MT 18:31 but that seg is verse-internal and I rely on it in neither direction.

reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 18:31-36 = MT 18:32-37. Selah note span-scoped and true. The row's rock-epithet claim is byte-true and I re-derived it rather than taking it on trust: MT 18:32 carries צ֝֗וּר, answering צ֭וּרִי at MT 18:3, so the interrogative reopening is real and the warrant is sound in itself. The closing boundary is also defensible as a boundary - MT 18:38 opens the 1cs sequence אֶרְדּ֣וֹף א֭וֹיְבַי. Two defects, both of them the shared property of a seam and therefore one edit installed on two rows. Defect one, the opening boundary: the span begins on a backward-binding particle clause and excludes the asyndetic verse that heads its own movement. That is the same seam contested on the adjacent row; I rate it medium here rather than high because this row inherits the boundary rather than authoring its displacement, and because this row's own warrant survives the correction unchanged and is in fact strengthened by it. Defect two, the contrast the row uses to justify its closing seam - second-person gift-verbs stopping at WEB 18:36 - is falsified three verses later by bytes inside the neighbouring span. Confidence medium is appropriate; the row's problem is its boundaries, not its reading.

challenges.claim: The span opens on a clause whose initial particle binds backward to the excluded preceding verse, and that excluded verse carries the divine designation and the perfect-way collocation that the span's own second verse completes.
challenges.evidence: web:Ps.18.30 = oshb:Ps.18.31, web:Ps.18.31 = oshb:Ps.18.32, web:Ps.18.32 = oshb:Ps.18.33 (shift+1); Hebrew spliced byte-true. MT 18:32 opens כִּ֤י, grounding the assertion of MT 18:31, and WEB keeps the connective: “For who is God, except Yahweh?” (web:Ps.18.31). MT 18:31 opens הָאֵל֮ and MT 18:33 opens הָ֭אֵל - identical at accent_stripped tier, differing at byte tier by accent placement only; 3 tokens over 3 verses in Ps 18 (MT 18:31, 18:33, 18:48). MT 18:31 reads תָּמִ֪ים דַּ֫רְכּ֥וֹ and MT 18:33 closes תָּמִ֣ים דַּרְכִּֽי, the same collocation at accent_stripped tier, so the span's SECOND verse completes a figure begun in the verse the span excludes - visible in WEB as “and makes my way perfect?” (web:Ps.18.32) answering “As for God, his way is perfect.” (web:Ps.18.30). The bounding epithet מָגֵ֥ן (2 tokens over 2 verses in Ps 18: MT 18:31 and MT 18:36 מָגֵ֪ן יִ֫שְׁעֶ֥ךָ) likewise closes inside this span but opens outside it. Moving the seam to WEB 18:29|18:30 leaves this row at WEB 18:30-36, policy-compliant, with its rock-epithet warrant intact and its frames no longer split.

challenges.claim: The closing-seam warrant asserts that second-person gift-verbs run no further than WEB 18:36 before shifting to the psalmist's own combat verbs, but the equipping collocation recurs in the second person 3 verses past the seam, including a token byte-identical across 2 verses, and neither row discloses it.
challenges.evidence: web:Ps.18.32 = oshb:Ps.18.33, web:Ps.18.34 = oshb:Ps.18.35, web:Ps.18.39 = oshb:Ps.18.40 (shift+1); Hebrew spliced byte-true. MT 18:33 reads הָ֭אֵל הַמְאַזְּרֵ֣נִי חָ֑יִל and MT 18:40 reads וַתְּאַזְּרֵ֣נִי חַ֭יִל לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה - the gird-plus-strength collocation repeated in 2ms form past the seam. Objects and units named: a contiguous consonantal sweep of the gird root over Ps 18 returns 2 tokens over 2 verses (MT 18:33, MT 18:40), though the two inflected spellings share no skeleton with each other and must be swept separately; the strength noun likewise returns 2 tokens over 2 verses (MT 18:33, MT 18:40) at skeleton tier. Strongest of all, the battle phrase is BYTE-identical at MT 18:35 and MT 18:40 - לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה at both, 2 tokens over 2 verses, collate tier byte. WEB carries the same second-person agency past the seam: “He teaches my hands to war,” (web:Ps.18.34) is answered by “For you have armed me with strength to the battle.” (web:Ps.18.39). The stated contrast therefore does not hold at the boundary it is used to justify. The seam may still stand on the 1cs sequence opening MT 18:38, but the warrant must be re-cut on both rows in one edit, and the replacement must survive this same test.

reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 18:37-42 = MT 18:38-43. Selah note span-scoped and true. The row's best argument is better than the row knows: the enemy-cry-unanswered inversion it asserts from English is carried in the bytes by a shared root - אֲשַׁ֫וֵּ֥עַ and וְ֝שַׁוְעָתִ֗י at MT 18:7 against יְשַׁוְּע֥וּ at MT 18:42, a contiguous consonantal sweep returning 4 tokens over 3 verses in Ps 18 (MT 18:7 twice, 18:42, 18:51) - and the row argues it from “he didn’t answer them.” (web:Ps.18.41) alone, leaving the original-language warrant unquoted where the standing rule asks for it. Both seams are sound: MT 18:38 opens the 1cs sequence אֶרְדּ֣וֹף, and MT 18:44 turns to 2ms address with תְּפַלְּטֵנִי֮. So the span stands and I do not contest it. What does not stand is the span DESCRIPTION, which asserts an unbroken continuity of voice that the bytes break twice in the middle of the span - and that same false contrast is what the neighbouring row uses to justify the shared seam, so the repair is one edit on both. Confidence high is overstated for a row whose stated distinguishing feature is falsified at 2 of its 6 verses.

challenges.claim: The claim that combat verbs in the psalmist's own voice run from web:Ps.18.37 through web:Ps.18.42 is falsified at web:Ps.18.39-18.40 = oshb:Ps.18.40-18.41, where the agency is second-person divine, and one of those verses repeats the equipping collocation of the preceding row across this row's own opening seam.
challenges.evidence: web:Ps.18.39 = oshb:Ps.18.40 and web:Ps.18.40 = oshb:Ps.18.41 (shift+1); Hebrew spliced byte-true. MT 18:40 reads וַתְּאַזְּרֵ֣נִי חַ֭יִל לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה תַּכְרִ֖יעַ קָמַ֣י תַּחְתָּֽי and MT 18:41 carries נָתַ֣תָּה - 2ms forms addressed to Yahweh, not 1cs forms of the psalmist. Object and unit named: of the 6 verses in this span, 2 verses (MT 18:40 and 18:41 = web:Ps.18.39 and 18:40) carry 2ms divine-agency verbs, so the asserted run is broken rather than continuous. WEB renders it the same way, so this is not a translation artifact and is visible at both witnesses: “For you have armed me with strength to the battle.” and “You have subdued under me those who rose up against me.” (web:Ps.18.39), then “You have also made my enemies turn their backs to me,” (web:Ps.18.40). The same verse also repeats the preceding row's equipping vocabulary across this row's opening seam: the battle phrase לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה at MT 18:40 is BYTE-identical to לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה at MT 18:35 (web:Ps.18.34), 2 tokens across 2 verses, and וַתְּאַזְּרֵ֣נִי at MT 18:40 repeats the gird-plus-strength figure of הַמְאַזְּרֵ֣נִי חָ֑יִל at MT 18:33 (web:Ps.18.32) - a cross-seam device that argues continuity with the prior strophe and is disclosed by neither row.
